name: Flexential Salt Lake City - South Valley

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Flexential Salt Lake City - South Valley publishes 1.2 MW of IT capacity across 30,512 square feet of technical space. Assuming 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density for mixed enterprise workloads, 1.2 MW supports roughly 120 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the same power budget supports only 30 racks. Neither figure is the operator's claim, and the ratio of square footage to power suggests the campus was designed for lower-density, general-purpose colocation rather than GPU-dense AI training.

The certification stack tells a specific story about intended workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify the campus for audited financial and operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR qualifies it to handle controlled defense-related technical data. HITRUST and NIST 800-53 qualify it for healthcare and federal-adjacent workloads. Taken together, the certifications position this campus for regulated enterprise tenants, not for hyperscale AI training, where compliance frameworks of this kind are rarely the primary selection criterion.

Among the 21 Utah facilities this site has mapped, only 8 publish a megawatt figure, and South Valley ranks eighth among those eight with 1.2 MW out of 51.69 MW of total published Utah capacity, a share of roughly 2.3 percent. It is the smallest published facility in the state by this measure. For a team evaluating Utah infrastructure for AI scale, this campus does not represent meaningful compute capacity on its own, but its regulatory certifications make it relevant for organizations that must run inference or data pipelines under ITAR, HIPAA-adjacent, or federal control frameworks.
